title: Vesper and the Tide
premise: Vesper Pemberton has spent ten years ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrated novelist Edmund Hale, while secretly writing anonymous letters to a stranger she met once on a night train—letters signed only 'Vesper.' When the stranger, Jonah Reyes, moves in next door and begins searching for the letter-writer he's loved from afar, Vesper must choose between protecting her invisibility and claiming the life she wrote for someone braver. As Edmund's memoir threatens to expose her authorship of both his words and the letters, Vesper discovers Jonah is dying and has come home to find her before time runs out. In the end, she lets him stay past the last train, confesses everything, and they build a final season together that outlasts even memory.
about_author: Ivo Marchetti is the pen name of a former railway station bookshop clerk who spent years listening to strangers' parting confessions on the platform. They write love stories set against timetables, tides, and the letters people almost send.

chapters.title: The Last Train Rule
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finishes ghostwriting chapter thirty of Edmund Hale's memoir, then walks to the station where ten years ago she missed a train and met a stranger. Establishes her rule: never stay past the last departure. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback to the night-train meeting and the first anonymous letter she sent. She's written one every month since, signed 'Vesper,' never expecting answers—but answers came. Beat: hope she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Moving trucks arrive next door; a man with a cane carries a box labeled with her old street address in another city. She recognizes Jonah Reyes from the train and panics. Beat: terror masquerading as curiosity.

chapters.title: Edmund's Deadline
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV at Edmund's townhouse. The publisher wants the memoir finished in four months; Edmund is charming, demanding, and increasingly forgetful. Beat: the quiet humiliation of being brilliant and unnamed.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He knocks on Vesper's door with a pretext about sugar, studying her face for recognition she won't give. He mentions, casually, that he's collecting letters. Beat: two people lying kindly to each other.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone, he unpacks 120 letters, rereading them, revealing his terminal diagnosis to the reader but not to Vesper. He came here because the postmark traced back. Beat: devotion sharpened by urgency.

chapters.title: Ghostwork
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A drafting session where Edmund claims her sentences as memories of his own; his editor praises 'his' voice. Vesper goes home hollow and starts a letter she doesn't send. Beat: erasure as a way of life.

chapters.title: Tide Charts
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Jonah asks Vesper to show him the coastal path; she agrees, telling herself it means nothing. The tide traps them briefly on a sandbar. Beat: involuntary intimacy.

chapters.title: What the Letters Said
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He quotes a letter aloud on the path without naming it; Vesper nearly betrays herself by finishing the sentence. She covers, badly. Beat: the mask cracking.

chapters.title: Edmund Remembers Her Wrong
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Edmund, confused, introduces her at a party as his 'research assistant' and tells a story she wrote as if it happened to him—with her in the audience of his fiction. Beat: grief for a self no one sees.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Garden
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Jonah plants a garden of flowers mentioned across all 120 letters; Vesper recognizes each one and realizes how much of herself she gave away. Beat: being known without consent—and wanting it anyway.

chapters.title: A Contract of Silence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Edmund offers her co-credit if she signs an NDA burying her role forever; money, security, continued invisibility. She almost signs. Beat: loyalty versus truth, first collision.

chapters.title: The Missed Connection
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He tells Vesper about the woman from the night train—the one who talked about tide charts and second chances—and watches her hands tremble. She leaves early. Beat: pursuit closing in.

chapters.title: Chapter Thirty-One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Writing Edmund's account of a marriage he neglected, she realizes she's ghosting her own life too. She writes Jonah's letter late at night, then burns it. Beat: self-recognition through another's story.

chapters.title: Rain on the Platform
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Stranded together under the station canopy during a storm, Jonah says he's running out of time; Vesper assumes he means the last train. Beat: dramatic irony as heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Editor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Edmund's editor notices stylistic inconsistencies between 'his' early chapters and recent ones, threatening exposure of the ghost arrangement. Beat: the professional trap tightening.

chapters.title: Jonah's Sister
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His sister arrives unannounced, furious he moved across the country to chase a decade of letters instead of entering treatment. She begs him to go home. Beat: love as opposition.

chapters.title: The Unsent Reply
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finds one of her own returned letters marked 'addressee unknown'—the first failure in ten years—and understands the correspondence was always a lifeline held by both ends. Beat: fear of losing what she never claimed.

chapters.title: Dinner That Wasn't a Date
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They cook together; Jonah sets a place for 'the letter-writer' out of habit. Vesper sits in her own empty chair metaphorically. Beat: domestic tenderness built on a secret.

chapters.title: Edmund's Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dictating half-lucid, Edmund admits he knows Vesper writes his life better than he lived it—and asks her to write him a redemption he didn't earn. Beat: complicity and contempt entwined.

chapters.title: The Hospital Corridor
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She finds Jonah collapsed outside his house; in the ambulance he grips her hand and says, 'Don't go before I find her.' Beat: stakes made physical.

chapters.title: Diagnosis
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the hospital he finally names his illness to Vesper: months, not years. He asks her help finding the letter-writer before the end. Beat: the secret becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: Why She Never Signed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback to her mother's death and the inheritance of silence—a family that taught her love was something you did anonymously. Beat: origin of the theme.

chapters.title: The Forged Chapter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. To save the memoir deadline she writes Edmund a childhood that never happened; it becomes the book's most praised passage. Beat: truth sacrificed beautifully, guilt blooming.

chapters.title: Almost Told
chapters.summary: Both POVs. On the pier at dusk, Vesper opens her mouth to confess twice; twice Jonah interrupts with kindness. Beat: the tragedy of bad timing she always believed in.

chapters.title: The Letter Count
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He counts his letters: one hundred twenty received, one hundred nineteen answered. One went astray—the returned one Vesper found. He fears she stopped writing. Beat: mutual misreading at maximum distance.

chapters.title: Sister's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His sister gives him forty-eight hours: enter the trial program in Boston or lose her support. Staying means dying here; leaving means dying unfound. Beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Edmund Reads the Letters
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Edmund discovers a stray letter in her manuscript pages and, lucid for once, tells her: 'Sign your name, girl. Outliving yourself is the only death.' Beat: unlikely mentorship.

chapters.title: The Trial Program
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Jonah decides to refuse treatment to spend his remaining time finding her; Vesper, hearing this, realizes her confession could either anchor him or break him. Beat: love weighing against survival.

chapters.title: Night Train, Again
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She boards the night train to Boston to intercept his sister, intending to leave a letter explaining everything—and can't do it. She rides back as dawn comes. Beat: courage failing at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Memoir Excerpt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The publisher releases an advance excerpt; critics hail Edmund's 'confession of a hidden love.' Readers begin hunting the real woman in the story—who is transparently her. Beat: exposure approaching from all sides.

chapters.title: Interview Request
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A journalist connects the memoir's heroine to the anonymous letters circulating online; Jonah sees the excerpt and recognizes their private language in print. Beat: the two secrets colliding publicly.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Townhouse
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Jonah arrives at Edmund's door mid-session, holding a letter, demanding to know why his words are in a famous man's memoir. Edmund covers for her—or claims her work as his own again. Beat: betrayal witnessed.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Believing Vesper sold their letters to Edmund for a career, he packs to leave for Boston. Vesper lets him go, convinced she's poison to everyone she touches. Beat: the false low point.

chapters.title: What Edmund Kept
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Dying Edmund reveals he intercepted and kept her very first letter years ago—he'd known about Jonah all along and feared losing his ghost. Beat: villainy revealed as fear; rage and release.

chapters.title: Platform Nine, Last Departure
chapters.summary: Climax, both POVs. Vesper runs to the station as Jonah's train pulls in, reads her first letter aloud over the loudspeaker system, and signs her name in front of the whole platform. He stays past the last train. Beat: visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They walk home along the tide line at midnight, trading truths: the diagnosis, the forged chapters, the intercepted letter. Forgiveness isn't instant, but it begins. Beat: honesty as intimacy.

chapters.title: Signing Her Name
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She demands credit on the memoir or withdraws entirely; the publisher, facing scandal, relents. The book ships with 'with Vesper Pemberton' on the cover. Beat: inheritance reclaimed—her own name.

chapters.title: The Season We're Given
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Autumn: the garden blooms out of season; Jonah enters a compassionate-care program nearby. They write letters again—this time handed directly, signed, read aloud. Beat: joy inside limitation.

chapters.title: Vesper and the Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. Spring. Jonah is gone; the memoir is hers; the garden persists. She teaches a ghostwriting workshop and tells students: sign everything. Final image—she stays on the platform after the last train, watching the tide come in, no longer counting departures. Beat: grief transmuted into presence.
